item.title: A Union Restored: New Zealand and the Cook Islands Repair Ties
item.description: From fallout to reset: how New Zealand and the Cook Islands navigated a dispute shadowed by China’s growing reach.

item.title: The Iranian Cyber Threat to U.S. Critical Infrastructure
item.description: U.S. agencies warn of Iranian cyber threats to critical infrastructure. This piece examines the cyber dimension of the U.S.-Iran conflict and U.S. cybersecurity's broader vulnerabilities—as kinetic war wages overseas, the homeland remains exposed.

item.title: Hungary After Orbán: The Hard Road Back to Democracy
item.description: The road back to democracy from authoritarianism is a difficult one, filled with fits and starts that thwart even the best attempts; Hungary holds some lessons for others trying to walk that path back to democracy.

item.title: Innovation Lightbulb: NSF’s Key Role in Economic and National Security
item.description: The NSF's mandate to secure the national defense, while often overlooked, has never been more relevant than it is today.

item.title: How to Interpret Wartime Oil Prices
item.description: Most oil market observers look to frequently quoted futures markets to represent the price of oil. But in the current supply disruption caused by the Iran war, the less publicized physical oil market is the best barometer of scarcity.

item.title: The Other China Flash Point
item.description: When imagining how the U.S.-Chinese relationship might devolve into war, experts often cite Taiwan as the most obvious flash point. In Foreign Affairs, Henrietta Levin argues that, like Taiwan, the South China Sea could spark a U.S.-China war.

item.title: Section 702: Why Do We Need It?
item.description: FISA Section 702 is up for renewal again. Congress renewed it in 2012, 2018, and 2024 with bipartisan support. Now, President Trump supports a clean reauthorization of the program. In other words, the government wants to extend it as it is, and it's the right policy.
